course.name: A2 Grammar: Everyday Accuracy with Nguyen Minh Ha
course.description: A cumulative A2 grammar pilot for accurate everyday communication.

lessons.title: Routines and Actions Now
lessons.objective: Choose the present simple for routines and facts and the present continuous for actions happening now.
lessons.description: Build the basic contrast between usual activities and events in progress.
lessons.content: The present simple describes habits, routines, and facts. The present continuous uses am, is, or are plus a verb ending in -ing for something happening now.
examples: I walk to work every day.
She is talking to her manager now.
commonErrors: Do not use is with a present-simple verb: She works here.
Do not omit be in the continuous: They are waiting.
lessons.guidedPractice: Underline the time clue, then choose the tense that matches the meaning.
lessons.summary: Use present simple for usual or true situations and present continuous for current temporary actions.

questions.questionText: My brother ___ breakfast at seven every morning.
questions.explanation: Every morning shows a regular routine, so use the present simple.

questions.questionText: Please be quiet. The baby ___ now.
questions.explanation: Now describes an action in progress, so use the present continuous.

questions.questionText: We ___ English on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
questions.explanation: A weekly schedule is a repeated routine, so use the present simple.

questions.questionText: Look! The bus ___ at the corner.
questions.explanation: Look signals an event happening at this moment.

questions.questionText: My parents ___ in Da Nang.
questions.explanation: A permanent fact uses the present simple.

questions.questionText: What ___ you ___ at the moment?
questions.explanation: At the moment asks about an action in progress: are you doing.

questions.questionText: Lan usually ___ tea, but today she ___ coffee.
questions.explanation: Usually is a habit while today describes a temporary action.

questions.questionText: The earth ___ around the sun.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact uses the present simple.

questions.questionText: They ___ dinner together tonight.
questions.explanation: Tonight describes a planned activity in the current period.

questions.questionText: I ___ this word. Can you explain it?
questions.explanation: Understand is normally used in the simple form for a current state.

lessons.title: Time Expressions and Context Clues
lessons.objective: Use common time expressions to select the correct present tense in everyday contexts.
lessons.description: Connect words such as always, usually, today, and right now to tense choices.
lessons.content: Frequency expressions often go with the present simple. Current-time expressions such as right now, this week, and today often go with the present continuous when the action is temporary or in progress.
examples: I am working from home this week.
commonErrors: Place always before the main verb but after be.
Do not choose a tense from one word alone; check whether the meaning is usual or temporary.
lessons.guidedPractice: Circle the time expression and explain whether the situation is usual, factual, or temporary.
lessons.summary: Time clues help, but meaning decides whether an action is a habit, fact, or current temporary event.

questions.questionText: Mai ___ her keys in the same drawer every day.
questions.explanation: Every day describes a repeated habit.

questions.questionText: This week, our team ___ a new project.
questions.explanation: This week presents a temporary current situation.

questions.questionText: He ___ late for class.
questions.explanation: Never expresses frequency and follows the verb be.

questions.questionText: Why ___ you ___ so fast today?
questions.explanation: Today describes the current unusual action.

questions.questionText: Our library ___ at eight every weekday.
questions.explanation: A regular opening time is a schedule or routine.

questions.questionText: I ___ with my cousin this month.
questions.explanation: This month describes a temporary arrangement.

questions.questionText: The train ___ at platform three every morning.
questions.explanation: Every morning indicates a repeated timetable.

questions.questionText: Listen! Someone ___ at the door.
questions.explanation: Listen points to an action happening now.

questions.questionText: We ___ lunch at noon on Sundays.
questions.explanation: On Sundays describes a regular routine.

questions.questionText: At present, the children ___ for their school play.
questions.explanation: At present means the activity is happening around now.

lessons.title: State and Action Verbs
lessons.objective: Avoid common A2 errors with verbs that normally describe states rather than temporary actions.
lessons.description: Practise know, like, want, need, understand, and remember in natural simple forms.
lessons.content: Many state verbs describe thoughts, feelings, possession, or needs. At A2 they normally use the present simple, even when the state is true now.
commonErrors: Prefer I know, not I am knowing.
Use does with he, she, and it in negative questions: Does he want tea?
lessons.guidedPractice: Decide whether each verb describes an action or a state before choosing the tense.
lessons.summary: Use the present simple with common state verbs for current thoughts, feelings, wants, and needs.

questions.questionText: She ___ the answer to this question.
questions.explanation: Know is a state verb and takes the present simple here.

questions.questionText: I ___ this film. It is very funny.
questions.explanation: Like describes a feeling and normally uses the simple form.

questions.questionText: Do you ___ any help?
questions.explanation: Need is a state verb used in the present simple question.

questions.questionText: My sister ___ a new phone.
questions.explanation: Want describes a current desire and takes the simple form.

questions.questionText: We ___ the way to the station.
questions.explanation: Remember is used in the simple form for a current state of memory.

questions.questionText: He ___ what you mean.
questions.explanation: Understand is normally a simple state verb.

questions.questionText: This bag ___ two large pockets.
questions.explanation: Have for possession uses the present simple.

questions.questionText: They ___ a break at the moment.
questions.explanation: Have can be continuous when it means taking an event or activity.

questions.questionText: Does your friend ___ spicy food?
questions.explanation: After does, use the base form like.

questions.questionText: I ___ a little tired today.
questions.explanation: Feel describes a current state and uses the simple form in this sentence.

lessons.title: Integrated Everyday Choices
lessons.objective: Choose the correct present tense in short everyday conversations and messages.
lessons.description: Combine form, time clues, and state/action distinctions in practical contexts.
lessons.content: Read the whole situation before choosing. Ask whether the speaker describes a usual fact, a temporary arrangement, an action now, or a state.
examples: I usually cycle, but I am taking the bus today.
We are meeting the teacher after class.
commonErrors: Do not select continuous only because the sentence is about today.
Check subject agreement: he works, but they work.
lessons.guidedPractice: Explain the meaning first, then select the form that matches the context.
lessons.summary: Accurate tense choice depends on both the time expression and the intended meaning.

questions.questionText: I usually walk, but today I ___ the bus.
questions.explanation: Today contrasts with the usual routine and describes a current choice.

questions.questionText: Our teacher ___ us homework every Friday.
questions.explanation: Every Friday describes a repeated classroom routine.

questions.questionText: Can I call later? We ___ lunch right now.
questions.explanation: Right now signals an action in progress.

questions.questionText: My aunt ___ in a hospital, but this month she ___ at home.
questions.explanation: Works is a usual fact; is resting is temporary this month.

questions.questionText: What time ___ the shop ___ on Saturdays?
questions.explanation: A timetable question uses does plus the base verb open.

questions.questionText: Look at Nam. He ___ a photo of the river.
questions.explanation: Look at identifies an action happening now.

questions.questionText: The café ___ good soup, so we often eat there.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes a regular fact about the café.

questions.questionText: This month, I ___ an evening English course.
questions.explanation: This month describes a temporary course arrangement.

questions.questionText: I ___ your point, but I need more information.
questions.explanation: Understand is a state verb and normally uses the present simple.

questions.questionText: Why ___ Minh ___ his jacket indoors today?
questions.explanation: Today describes a current unusual action: is wearing.
